mechanics.name: Exultation
mechanics.currentEffect: While you are holding an Item, stunning the Killer by dropping a Pallet recharges the Item by 75% and upgrades its Rarity to the next available tier. Exultation then has a 30/25/20-second cooldown. An Item already at maximum rarity cannot be upgraded and therefore does not receive this recharge.
activation: You must be holding an Item.
You must stun the Killer by dropping a Pallet.
Ends/deactivates when: The perk cannot trigger while on cooldown.
mechanics.patchNote: Latest live balance change (9.0.0): Increased Item recharge from 25% to 75% and reduced cooldown from 40/35/30 to 30/25/20 seconds.
mechanics.plainEnglishSummary: A Pallet stun while holding an Item improves and recharges it, then puts the perk on cooldown.
specialInteractions: An Item at maximum Rarity cannot advance to the next tier, so the recharge effect does not occur for that trigger.

editorial.summary: A pallet stun upgrades your held Item by one rarity and, when upgraded, restores a large portion of its Charges.
useCases: Upgrade a weaker Toolbox, Med-Kit, or Flashlight while simultaneously recharging it.
Turn successful pallet stuns into long-term resource value.
Pair with item-centered builds where extra Charges matter throughout the Trial.
counters: An already maximum-rarity Item cannot be upgraded and therefore does not receive the recharge.
You must still bring or find an Item worth improving.
pros: Can improve both rarity and remaining resource pool.
Short cooldown if repeated stuns are available.
cons: No value with a max-rarity Item.
analysis: Exultation ranks this position because its modern 75% recharge can be a serious resource swing. A successful pallet stun can both upgrade the Item and return most of its charges, creating far more value than the perk's original version.

The best targets are Items whose additional charges translate directly into time or survival, such as Toolboxes and Med-Kits. The pallet stun becomes more than a chase win; it becomes a resource refresh that continues paying afterward.

The restriction around maximum rarity matters. Once the Item can no longer upgrade, the recharge component stops being available through the same interaction, limiting repeated use with already-premium gear.

Exultation is therefore a strong build-around perk rather than general utility. Players who plan around an upgradeable Item and land stuns can extract impressive value; everyone else should choose something more reliable.
editorial.verdict: A strong item-economy reward for successful pallet play. Exultation can generate huge resource value, but only if your Item still has somewhere to upgrade.
